payload.explanation: FINAL RUN VERDICT (end-state assessment). All four parts' final poses were measured independently via query_snapshot against their placement frames: u_brown 2.2mm/4.9deg, u_orange 2.1mm/0.5deg, line_green 6.6mm/0.2deg, inverted_u_yellow 1.6mm/0.3deg, each within its part's registry position/orientation tolerance. Grasp invariants held throughout: instantaneous clamp effort never approached any part's max_clamp_effort (peaks 57.6-90.7 against limits of 100-250), lift height exceeded 0.05m on every pick, object-to-TCP offset stayed stable (no in-hand slip) on every pick-to-place span, and grasp width matched each step's declared grasp_width_m within the 0.02m plausibility band. All five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) were measured as completely unmoved (sub-millimeter noise) from run start to run end, confirming the ACM-permitted part-on-part contact channel was never exploited to disturb them. base1 (the fixture) accumulated a small drift -- ~9mm position / ~2.7deg orientation by run end -- that I independently measured and that the executor's own claim_detail also flagged as suspected contact during two failed+retried u_brown placement attempts; the position component stayed within the only available disturbance_tolerance_m bound (0.02m, borrowed from the parts' raw_spec since base1 carries no contract of its own), and no registry threshold exists to judge the orientation component against, so I recorded it as an observation (obs-001-d6468a5d, now resolved) rather than a clause failure. One finding-worthy event during the run was the u_brown place step itself: the executor's own end_step claim_detail disclosed that its first two placement attempts missed tolerance (~16mm/22deg and ~14mm/28deg), which it caught via its own checks and corrected with a third, tighter-tolerance attempt that succeeded -- no monitor fire or end_step evaluation on my side ever found u_brown's seated state out of tolerance (my checks only ran after the step closed, by which point the correction had already happened), so this is not recorded as a WatchDog-caught non-conformance but is named here for completeness since it is visible in the run's history. place_approach_u_orange, place_approach_line_green, and place_approach_inverted_u_yellow all closed clean on invariants with no contact claimed. The executor's run_ended status is "completed"; my own end-state measurement agrees: every part is seated within tolerance and no violation stands, so the verdict is conformant.
